doc.title: Walter Booker and Jimmy Cobb interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995

title: Unspoken communication and camaraderie on the bandstand
summary: Woods asks about who sparks a night; Booker says everyone feels it should be them, so nobody knows who created the energy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know there is, in listening to the groups that I admire, there seems to be an unspoken communication in jazz, night after night on the bandstand. It seems to be and I want you all to elaborate on this, times when the energy level is a little bit higher that night than it used to be, or one person takes off, one person says, well, you know somebody’s looking for somebody to get it started. You say we all know we can play, we all know that we’re more than proficient players, but who feels like stepping out tonight? And then somebody says okay I’m going to be the spark plug tonight. You know and somebody takes a real nice solo, and then everybody comes up behind him.
I just want you to talk about the camaraderie that takes place on stage.

If you have that attitude about it, if everybody felt that way, let’s say you were serious, well that’d be me because that would be me too, I feel like I’d need to be the one to do that. If everybody feels that way then you will never know and we will never know either which one created that hype, I mean that variable that you’re speaking of. You never know which one. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
Well I guess our engagement, I guess we can all figure each other out, one way or the other.
